summary: Comprehensive backend testing of Geofence Attendance Console. 35/35 pytest tests passing covering auth (register-org, login, /me, refresh rotation, logout, forgot/reset, 5-attempt lockout), offices CRUD with tenant isolation, employees CRUD (uniqueness + invalid office rejection + soft delete), sessions state machine (low accuracy 400, outside geofence 403 with 'Signing denied', successful start with 3,600,000ms remaining, duplicate 400, admin-cannot-start), ping pause/resume with bout increment, reset writes attendance record, hash chain continuity across records, CSV+PDF exports with proper headers, audit log + security events (admin-only), and org settings persistence with role enforcement.

minor.issue: Access token issued during refresh can be byte-identical to the previous one when refresh happens within the same second because the JWT payload (sub, email, org_id, role, type, exp) has second-resolution `exp` and no `iat`/`jti`. Consider adding `iat` or a random `jti` to access tokens so rotated tokens are always distinct. Not a security bug — refresh_token IS rotated + revoked correctly — but a minor observability improvement.

Returns `{ok: true, sent: <bool>}` — the extra `sent` field leaks whether the email exists in the org (true for known emails, false for unknown). Should omit `sent` or always return the same shape to avoid user enumeration.

When status is 'active' and the new ping is OUTSIDE the geofence, the code still subtracts (now-last).dt from remaining_ms BEFORE transitioning to paused. That means one full ping interval of outside-time is counted as inside-time. Consider transitioning first, then counting only up to the boundary crossing.

action_items: Consider adding `iat` or `jti` claim to access tokens so refresh always produces a distinct token string.
Remove `sent` boolean from /api/auth/forgot-password response to avoid user enumeration.
Revisit /api/sessions/ping remaining_ms accounting when transitioning active→paused (currently counts the outside interval as inside).
critical_code_review_comments: seed.py rehashes admin password on every startup if it differs — good, matches playbook.
bcrypt hashes generated correctly via passlib (verified via successful login).
httpOnly + Secure + SameSite=None cookies set on login, register-org, refresh; cleared on logout — matches spec.
CORS uses explicit origins from env with allow_credentials=True — correct for cookie-based auth.
Tenant isolation verified: office IDs from Org A are invisible to Org B users and PATCH/DELETE returns 404.
Hash chain (record_hash + prev_record_hash) verified deterministic and correctly linked across sequential records.
MongoDB `_id` correctly excluded from all API responses (shaped via helper functions).
Server-authoritative session state machine — client cannot manipulate remaining_ms directly.

Anti-spoof: low accuracy triggers 400 with 'accuracy' message and logs low_accuracy_start; geofence violation triggers 403 with 'Signing denied' and logs geofence_denied — both observed in /api/security-events.
Employee role-guard is correct: employees cannot list/create employees, offices (POST), org settings PATCH, audit-log, security-events, attendance exports.
